chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Learning to arrange from Henderson and Ellington records
summary: Smith copied Fletcher Henderson's keys from records, and Henderson once corrected the key of Yeah Man in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Actually, this takes me back to the other thing about you, which is very interesting. Because you're a great arranger. How did you learn to do that? When did it start, and how and why? When did you get interested in it?

Well, I listened to the Fletcher Henderson and Duke Ellington bands. You listen to them... I know Fletcher was writing all the arrangements... I would get his records. I found out that he was... That the beautiful numbers, he had a technique going. He wrote some numbers that would sound so pretty, especially those ballad numbers, sweet numbers. He'd put them in a certain key to get that weird sound, and let Hawk take them solos. Like, he had "Talk Of The Town" -- he had in D-natural. See, a lot of fellows didn't know it. And I would copy it off,

and find out where it was...
Then, at one time, we had a (?) moment that he was playing in Kansas City, and he came in. They got through playing that night, and we was playing at the Cherry Blossom with the Bennie Moten band. I remember a number called "Yeah Man," one of those fast numbers, a little like that [PATS TEMPO]. And they got through playing and they came into the house; all the band sat and listened to us play. So Fletcher got up and got (?)talked to Basie(?) ...(?). by the band. I'd been counting that number off, copied it and put it in A-flat. And Fletcher faced around, and I don't know who told him, but he looked right straight at me, (?)Basie, I think(?), and said, "You've got it in A-flat; it's in G." And Basie looked up at me and said "I told you so." I said, "You ain't told me nothin'."
Could Fletcher tell key was being played?
Yeah. I learned that myself. I ...(?).(?). and it looked like they weren't paying attention to what key they were playing in. I'm talking about the sound of the horns.
Good Lord, that's amazing. Actually, it's quite true. Different keys do sound...
